title: Twelve of 85 M3+ events in an Oklahoma box in 2021-2025 followed two years without a detected M2.5+ event within 5 km
abstract: We test spatial persistence and local detected quiet periods in a fixed USGS ComCat snapshot. The study box is 34-37 N, 99.6-95.9 W. In 2021-2025, 64 of 85 M3+ events lie within 5 km of a 2010-2016 M3+ epicentre. Twelve of the 85 events follow more than two years without a detected M2.5+ event within 5 km; five follow more than five years. At 10 km, the counts are seven and three. Using M3+ history instead increases the 5 km two-year count to 26. A spatial kernel comparison with years as permutation units does not resolve a change from 2014-2016 to 2021-2025 at M3+ (p = 17/56 at 10 km scale). An M2.5+ signal is scale dependent. These results show that local detected quiet and later activity can coexist near an earlier footprint. They do not measure a restart probability per fault, identify the residual driver, or measure the ETAS taper. Limits include few years, unequal annual counts, annual-map exchangeability, catalog completeness, magnitude changes and location error. The package provides code, exact source provenance, aggregate evidence, figures, and an independent arithmetic audit. Source records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Local detected quiet periods before 85 M3+ events in the study box in 2021-2025. History uses M2.5+ events from 2010. Targets without earlier neighbours have censored gaps; their survival mass remains beyond the plot range.
